record.category: push notification API for iOS, Android and web browsers (hosted)

free_tier.stated: Beams Sandbox plan, priced Free: 1,000 subscribers (registered devices) and Standard support
free_tier.notes: A subscriber is a device registered to receive notifications. The count is the sum of concurrent subscribers across all Beams instances for a given day. A device counts from the SDK start call until the stop call, or until the platform gateway invalidates its token. Reinstalling an app on a device adds a new subscriber until the cleanup removes the old one. The pricing page names no notification count, and an older tutorial says a free plan can send unlimited push notifications to up to 1000 devices. The next plan is Startup at USD 29 a month for 10,000 subscribers.

per_object_cap.stated: 10 KiB request body on a publish to interests; 200 KiB request body on a publish to users
per_object_cap.notes: The two publish endpoints have different caps, so no single byte count is recorded. The body carries the target list and the payload for each platform.

retention.stated: An undelivered notification expires at the platform gateway after its time-to-live: at most 4 weeks on web push and FCM, and the payload expiration timestamp on APNs. A device registration stays until the SDK stop call or until the gateway invalidates the token
retention.notes: Web push accepts a time-to-live of at most 2419200 seconds and defaults to 4 weeks. FCM takes at most 4 weeks, which is also its default. APNs takes an expiration timestamp in the payload. 4 weeks is 28 days (4 x 7).

egress.terms: not stated: the pricing page lists subscribers and a support level and names no notification count, byte allowance or price per notification

record.interface_detail: Publish API: HTTPS POST to INSTANCE_ID.pushnotifications.pusher.com under /publish_api/v1/instances/INSTANCE_ID/publishes/interests or /publishes/users, with a JSON body and the instance secret key as a Bearer token. Devices register through the Android, iOS and Web SDKs, which call the Device API on the same host.
record.tooling: Official client SDKs for Android, iOS, Web (JavaScript) and Flutter; official server SDKs for Go, PHP, Node.js, Python, Java and Kotlin, Ruby and Swift; or any HTTP client that posts JSON with the instance secret key. A web page needs a service worker file, served over HTTPS, that imports the hosted Beams worker script.
record.chaining: A worker on any free compute service posts one HTTPS request to the Publish API to reach up to 1,000 registered browsers and phones, and Pusher Channels covers live updates to open pages.

limits.value: 1,000 subscribers (registered devices, counted as concurrent subscribers across all Beams instances for a given day)
100 requests per second to the Publish API; a request above the rate answers 429
10 KiB request body on a publish to interests; 200 KiB on a publish to users
notification time-to-live of at most 2419200 seconds (4 weeks) on web push and at most 4 weeks on FCM

record.limits_note: A publish to interests names 1 to 100 interests and a publish to users names 1 to 1000 user IDs. A device holds at most 5000 interests and a user holds at most 100 devices per platform. The vocabulary has no kind for a count cap, so the subscriber cap is filed as volume-quota.
record.binding_note: The 1,000-subscriber cap is the only plan threshold on the pricing page, and it counts registered devices, not bytes, so a growing app meets it before the Publish API rate of 100 requests a second.

identity_cost.detail: The Pusher sign-up form asks for an email address and a password, or a GitHub or Google sign-in, behind an invisible reCAPTCHA, and has no phone or card field; a Beams instance is then created in the dashboard. Android delivery needs an FCM service account file from a Firebase project, iOS delivery needs an APNs key from an Apple Developer account, and Safari delivery needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership. The web SDK guide for Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Opera uses only the instance ID and secret key from the dashboard.

record.reliability_note: Over the subscriber cap a publish answers 402 after a 7-day notice period and no notification is delivered, while device registration still succeeds; Standard support has best-effort response times, and the status page lists Beams and the Beams dashboard as Operational on 2026-11-01.
record.confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from first-party pricing, documentation and support pages. The Publish API host answered 405 to a GET on its POST-only route, and the hosted web service worker script answered 200. No notification was published, because publishing needs an instance ID and secret key, which only an account holds; a publish with a Sandbox key would move this record to measured. unverified: whether the first Beams instance asks for a card, how many instances a Sandbox account may hold and whether an idle Sandbox instance expires, because the Beams dashboard is behind a sign-up.

card.category: realtime pub/sub messaging over WebSocket with an HTTP publish API
card.summary: Channels Sandbox: 200k messages per day and 100 concurrent connections, free

record.category: realtime pub/sub messaging over WebSocket with an HTTP publish API

free_tier.stated: Channels Sandbox: 200k messages per day and 100 concurrent connections, free
free_tier.notes: A message is each API request plus each delivery to a connected client: a publish to 50 subscribers is 51 messages. Limits are counted per account, over all the apps it owns. A warning email goes out at 80% of a limit. Past the daily message limit every trigger request answers 403 over quota; past the connection limit new connections are rejected, and on Sandbox the connection limit is enforced at once (paid plans at 120%). One trigger request reaches at most 100 channels.

per_object_cap.stated: 10KB of event data per message; a larger event answers 413
per_object_cap.notes: The page writes 10KB without saying 10,000 or 10,240 bytes, so no byte count is recorded.

retention.stated: No message history by default; an opt-in cache channel keeps the last event in memory for at most 30 minutes or until a new event arrives

egress.terms: Each delivery to a connected client counts as a message against the 200k daily quota; no byte allowance is stated

record.interface_detail: HTTP API at api-CLUSTER.pusher.com (for example api-mt1.pusher.com) over HTTP or HTTPS, each request signed with an HMAC SHA256 digest; clients hold WebSocket connections to ws-CLUSTER.pusher.com on port 80 for ws or 443 for wss, with an HTTP fallback transport, which the interface vocabulary has no term for.
record.tooling: The pusher-js client and the Pusher server libraries, or any HTTP client that signs requests with the app secret.
record.chaining: A notification fan-out from a worker to a browser dashboard, sized for about 18,000 publishes a day to 10 subscribers each.

limits.value: 200k messages per day per account, deliveries included
no history; cache channels keep the last event for at most 30 minutes

record.limits_note: 100 concurrent connections per account, enforced at once on Sandbox, and 100 channels per trigger request. The vocabulary has no kind for a concurrency cap.
record.binding_note: A publish to n subscribers counts n + 1 against 200,000 a day, so a publish to 10 subscribers leaves about 18,000 publishes a day (200,000 / 11); a fan-out to more than 100 clients meets the connection cap first.

identity_cost.detail: The signup form asks for an email address and a password, or a GitHub or Google sign-in, behind an invisible reCAPTCHA; billing and card details are entered only when a plan is upgraded.

record.reliability_note: Over the daily message quota the HTTP API answers 403 and further publishes fail until the next day; connections over the limit are rejected at once on Sandbox.
record.confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from first-party pricing, documentation and support pages; the HTTP API host was probed and answered 400 to an unsigned request. No event was published, because publishing needs an app key and secret. A signed publish from a Sandbox app would move it to measured.
